assumptions: source assumption: Wright-Fisher ideal population in all respects EXCEPT the 1:1 sex ratio (random mating, Poisson-distributed family sizes, constant breeder number, no migration/mutation/selection); Ne is the ideal-population size losing heterozygosity (UWyo) or drifting (Wikipedia) at the observed rate.

source assumption: Nm and Nf count BREEDING males and females contributing to the next generation (dairy-cow 'breeding herd'), not the raw census; overlapping generations and variance-skewed success need the fuller treatments.
source assumption: single-generation, discrete-generation framing (Wright 1931/1938 lineage).

gaps: Quantity meanings breeding_males, breeding_females and effective_size are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot; runtime projection omitted.

models.inverse_notes: Breeding-male count is recoverable as Nm = Ne*Nf / (4*Nf - Ne) for 4*Nf != Ne. Substitution check: 64*20 / (80 - 64) = 1280/16 = 80, consistent with the 80/20 reference. Single-sex breeding (Nm = 0 or Nf = 0) is excluded by the guards (the ratio is undefined); the 1000-to-1 near-boundary illustrates Ne collapsing toward 4 times the rarer sex.
limitations: Sex-ratio correction only; variance in reproductive success, fluctuating size, overlapping generations and spatial structure reduce Ne through the separate treatments, not this record.
Ne is a drift/inbreeding rate parameter, not a head count: Ne below N does not mean individuals are missing.

references.method: Published worked example: Ne = 4 x 80 x 20 / (80 + 20) = 6400/100 = 64, stated to be less than the census N = 100.
references.provenance: Published result (worked example with exact integer arithmetic).

references.method: Published dairy-cow example: 96 cows and 4 bulls give 4 x 96 x 4 / 100 = 1536/100 = 15.36; the lecture reports the rounded 15.4, so the expected keeps the exact recomputation (difference 0.04 documented here).
references.provenance: Published result (lecture example) kept at exact recomputation with documented rounding of the reported 15.4.

references.method: Published sanity check from the UWyo lecture ('Try putting 50:50 in Eqn 7.5 to verify that Ne = N when the sex ratio is 1:1'): 4*50*50/100 = 100 = N, exact.
references.provenance: Published result (lecture's printed verification case) matched by exact integer arithmetic.

rejection_cases.reason: With zero breeding males the sex-ratio formula has no finite effective size.
Breeding-female count Nf is required; males alone do not determine the effective size.

relationship.locator: Wikipedia 'Non-Fisherian sex-ratios': 'Ne(v) = Ne(F) = 4NmNf/(Nm + Nf). Where Nm is the number of males and Nf the number of females.' with the worked 80/20 -> 64; UWyo Lecture 7 prints the dairy-cow application (96 cows, 4 bulls -> effective size 15.4) and the 50:50 sanity check (Ne = N at 1:1).
relationship.translation_notes: Source symbols Nm, Nf, Ne preserved. Dimensional check: count times count over count gives a count of ideal individuals. The factor 4 is exact combinatorics of the two-sex diploid derivation, kept inline with this note rather than as a fitted constant. Equal-ratio identity: Nm = Nf gives Ne = Nm + Nf = N (verified UWyo sanity check).

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: with sex ratio varying from Fisherian 1:1, Ne(v) = Ne(F) = 4NmNf/(Nm + Nf) with Nm males and Nf females; worked 80 males and 20 females gives 6400/100 = 64, less than N = 100; Ne introduced by Wright 1931 as the idealised-population size drifting at the observed rate.

assumptions: source assumption: the stated allele frequencies exhaust the gene pool at the locus (source: frequencies 'added up to 100 percent').

models.inverse_notes: Any one allele frequency is recoverable given all others (e.g. f1 = 1 - f2 - f3); the record fixes f3 as output only as the serialization choice. Substitution check: 1 - 0.261 - 0.134 = 0.605, consistent with the ABO reference. Fixation of one allele (the rest zero) gives 1 and is admissible.
limitations: Multi-allele loci only in the three-allele serialization; loci with more alleles need the fuller summation, not recorded here.
A bookkeeping complement, not an equilibrium prediction; it holds regardless of evolutionary forces.
Published percentage triples may not sum to exactly 100.0 (the mosquito pre-treatment triple sums to 99.9); affected references carry the rounding in their tolerances.

references.method: Published Jordanian ABO study figures quoted on the page: IA 26.1 percent and IB 13.4 percent leave 1 - 0.261 - 0.134 = 0.605 for I0, matching the quoted 60.5 percent.
references.provenance: Published result (printed allele frequencies of the cited study) recombined through the summation constraint.

references.method: Constructed check: 1 - 0.5 - 0.25 = 0.25 by direct subtraction; verifies encoding, no field value claimed.
references.provenance: Independently constructed arithmetic check; not a published field value.

references.method: Published Equatorial Guinea mosquito resistance-allele triple (6.3, 74.6, 19.0 percent): 1 - 0.063 - 0.746 = 0.191 against the reported 19.0 percent; the 0.001 gap is the source's own rounding (printed triple sums to 99.9), carried in the 0.002 tolerance.
references.provenance: Published result (field-study percentages quoted on the AP page) kept at the reported value with documented rounding propagation.

references.method: Published post-treatment mosquito triple (11.1, 83.3, 5.6 percent): 1 - 0.111 - 0.833 = 0.056 exact, matching the reported 5.6 percent; shows the summation holding after two years of selection-driven change.
references.provenance: Published result (field-study percentages quoted on the AP page) matched by exact decimal arithmetic.

rejection_cases.reason: Allele frequencies summing above 1 (0.7 + 0.5 = 1.2) cannot come from one gene pool.
Second allele frequency f2 is required; one allele alone does not determine the complement.

relationship.locator: Section 19.1 'Population Genetics': ABO example with 'a frequency of IA to be 26.1 percent', 'IB and I0 alleles comprise 13.4 percent and 60.5 percent respectively, and all of the frequencies added up to 100 percent'.

relationship.translation_notes: Summation constraint for the three-allele case solved for the third frequency; symbols f1, f2, f3 introduced (the page uses prose and percentages). Dimensional check: pure number minus dimensionless frequencies gives a dimensionless frequency. This is a distinct relationship from the two-allele complement (different arity and scope), not a rearrangement of it.
